text: For a planar linear system x' = A x, if the eigenvalues of A are real and of opposite sign, the equilibrium at the origin is a:
explanation: Real eigenvalues of opposite sign produce a saddle: attracting along one eigendirection and repelling along the other, hence unstable. Two negative real eigenvalues give a stable node, purely imaginary eigenvalues give a center, and complex eigenvalues with nonzero real part give a spiral.
